---
title: "Practical work and communication"
---

These activities form a first classroom teaching draft. They use supplied
textual observations and simulated datasets; core analysis works with paper
and a calculator. They support but do not replace established laboratory
protocols, actual specimens or supervised practical skills sessions. Formal
assessment rules and local protocols come from the teaching team.

## Your route

| Activity | Focus | Suggested working time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Anatomy and histology](anatomy-histology.qmd) | Evidence for tissue identity and comparative structure/function | 75–90 min plus actual specimen practice |
| [Animal oxygen consumption](animal-measurements.qmd) | Background correction, units, temperature and metabolism | 90 min |
| [Plant water balance](plant-water.qmd) | Mass balance, area normalisation and water potential | 90 min |
| [Photosynthetic light response](photosynthesis.qmd) | Repeated readings, compensation and net/gross exchange | 90 min |
| [Growth and stress](development-stress.qmd) | Within-plant change, treatment comparison and mechanisms | 90 min |
| [Scientific reporting](reporting.qmd) | Scientific argument and peer review | Drafting and revision sessions |
| [Literature and presentation](literature-presentation.qmd) | Critical reading, biotechnology and ethics | Preparation, group discussion and presentation |

Times are planning suggestions, not booked contact hours. Accompany the
corresponding animal/plant lessons rather than creating a computing block.
Keep the [simulated-data dictionary](../data/README.md) with each CSV. Compare
your first plot with the [worked-figure gallery](../figures.qmd).

## Anatomy and histology

Observe representative normal tissues and organs, recognise characteristic
features and explain how structure supports function. Retain comparisons
between animal groups and the established specimen sessions.

## Physiological experiments

Carry out the course's established animal and plant experiments. Identify
the question, experimental unit, controls, measurements and units before
interpreting results. Preserve observations and distinguish variation among
organisms from repeated measurements of one organism.

The local practical manual, equipment, specimens and timetable determine live
experiments. Supplied classroom observations do not verify specimen-handling
or experimental skills.

## Scientific reporting

A report should connect the physiological question, methods, results and
interpretation. Explain figures, uncertainty and limitations rather than
presenting numbers alone. No R is required. An
[optional supplied R walkthrough](../optional-computing/index.qmd) repeats
the animal analysis if the teacher trials computing within existing analysis time.

## Literature and presentation

Read scientific evidence critically, discuss physiological mechanisms and
communicate a reasoned interpretation orally and in writing. Plant
biotechnology discussion includes potential benefits, risks and ethics.
